concepts.title: Why Social Science: The Four Themes

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Why Social Science: The Four Themes' refers to.
questions.a: Social science studies human life through four connected themes: the land and people of India, the tapestry of the past, our cultural heritage and knowledge traditions, and governance with economic life around us.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Why Social Science: The Four Themes'.
questions.a: Society is studied through themes that link place, history, culture and governance.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Why Social Science: The Four Themes' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Maps and the Globe' refers to.
questions.a: A map is a drawing of a place as seen from above, using symbols and signs; a globe is a small round model of the Earth, and both help us locate places and see the world at a glance.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Maps and the Globe'.
questions.a: Maps shrink large places onto paper so that streets, towns and countries can be studied together.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Maps and the Globe' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Introduction, map activity (source: fees101.txt, Introduction, map activity)

concepts.title: The Four Arrows: Directions on a Map

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Four Arrows: Directions on a Map' refers to.
questions.a: The four arrows at the corner of a map point to the cardinal directions, north, south, east and west; they fix every place on the map relative to every other place.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Four Arrows: Directions on a Map'.
questions.a: Directions turn a flat drawing into a usable map: once north is fixed, every other direction follows.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Four Arrows: Directions on a Map' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Introduction, map reading (source: fees101.txt, Introduction, map reading)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Society, Governance and Economic Life' refers to.
questions.a: The introduction shows that society works because families, communities, governments and economic activities support one another; social science studies each strand and the threads that join them.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Society, Governance and Economic Life'.
questions.a: No part of social life stands alone: living together needs governance, culture and work.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Society, Governance and Economic Life' taught, and from which source text?
